_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the consumer-facing devflow -> prflow rename (issue #1002 Tier 1, whose scope supersedes issue #988's config-key-only scope, plus issue #1003 Tier 2's top-level identifiers block). Every site that has to know a superseded name resolves it from here rather than carrying its own literal copy: scripts/scaffold-config.sh's config-key migration, scripts/config-get.sh's superseded-key probe, scripts/migrate-consumer-tier1.sh's four-member atomic unit, and the workflow config-job guards (pinned against this table at desk time by lib/test/run.sh rather than read at runtime, because a workflow's inline jq cannot load a file the checkout may not carry). There is no shared loader helper: every reader parses this file itself — the three named above, plus lib/test/pin-corpus-lint.py, which builds the desk-time rename substitution from it. Two files deliberately do NOT read it and mirror it instead: lib/resolve-state-dir.sh and lib/state_dir.py carry the `paths.state_dir` literals, because a .sh cannot be sourced by the Python readers and a .py cannot be sourced into a shell; the tier1-rename-migration suite module asserts all three agree. The frozen block is enumerated so a later sweep cannot 'helpfully' widen the map -- adding a member there is a behaviour change with its own issue, never a tidy-up.

paths.renamed_subtrees_comment: Read ONLY by lib/test/pin-corpus-lint.py's desk-time rename substitution -- NOT by the consumer migration, which resolves paths.state_dir/vendor_dir by name and never enumerates this block. Each entry records a one-off in-repo `git mv` of a subtree (unrelated to the devflow->prflow brand rename) so a pin whose only change is that respelling is not read as a re-pointed pin. Issue #152 moved the reception skill to skills/fix and its prompt-extension to fix.md. Issue #170 renamed the consumer-facing extension directory .prflow/prompt-extensions -> .prflow/skill-extensions; the reception-skill file entry below carries the current .prflow/skill-extensions/fix location, and the longest-first ordering makes it out-compete the bare directory rule on a reception-skill pin.

identifiers.detail: The GitHub provenance label (issue #1003). `token` match, so the unrelated compound `DevFlow-layout` and every prose occurrence of the product name are out of reach: a token rule refuses to fire when the next character continues the token, and `-` counts as a continuation.

The telemetry branch and the artifact names derived from it (issue #1003). `prefix` match, because the shipped names extend it with a hyphen -- `devflow-telemetry-stage-<run>` -- which a token rule would refuse.

The `<!-- devflow:* -->` comment-marker namespace (issue #1003). `prefix` match, and it is deliberately NARROWER than the bare `devflow:` namespace: the plugin's subagent-override keys (`devflow:code-reviewer`) and the transitional command spellings (`/devflow:implement`) keep the old namespace as a permanent accepted alias, so only the marker form -- which always opens with the HTML comment token -- is renamed.

atomic_unit.title: state directory move
atomic_unit.detail: the consumer's .devflow/ tree, including its vendor/devflow subdirectory, relocated to .prflow/ (vendor/prflow) with every byte preserved

atomic_unit.title: workflow-content rewrite
atomic_unit.detail: every .github/workflows/*.yml present on disk that names a superseded path or config key, rewritten in place; the workflow FILENAMES are frozen

atomic_unit.title: marketplace-source rewrite
atomic_unit.detail: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json's local plugin source (and the description that names the same path) repointed at the current vendor dir

atomic_unit.title: plugin version pin
atomic_unit.detail: the consumer's plugin pin renamed devflow_version -> prflow_version and advanced to a ref that contains this layout, so the runtime-vendored plugin and the migrated tree agree

env_identifiers.policy: AN INVENTORY OF NAMES NOT TO RENAME. This block is NOT a rename table and must never be rendered, summarised or quoted as one. The consumer-facing DEVFLOW_* variables, secrets and environment overrides below are FROZEN under their DEVFLOW_ spelling: no PRFLOW_* read side exists anywhere in the tree, so each name is read under that spelling and only under that spelling. Renaming one does not move a setting -- it deletes it, and most of these delete it SILENTLY (each row's failure_visibility is the answer for that row; do not restate a count here, it rots the moment a row is added or its visibility is re-judged). Only a later tier that ships an actual dual read (PRFLOW_* preferred, DEVFLOW_* still accepted) can unfreeze a row, and it unfreezes it HERE, in the same change that ships the read.

criterion._comment: An identifier is consumer-facing iff arm A1 or arm A2 selects it. Both arms are mechanical and are implemented by `lib/generate-env-freeze-advisory.py --derive`, which the tier1-rename-migration module runs against the live tree and reconciles with this block: a name the arms select that appears in neither `identifiers` nor `adjudicated_out` turns the suite RED, and so does a recorded name the arms no longer select. So a workflow that starts reading a new vars./secrets. name, or a doc that starts declaring a new operator override, cannot enter or leave the consumer surface without an adjudication recorded here.
criterion.A1: Cloud channel -- the name appears as `secrets.<NAME>` or `vars.<NAME>` in a workflow install.sh ships. The consumer sets it in GitHub repository/organization settings; the tree can only read it.
criterion.A2: Operator channel -- the name is read as an ambient environment variable (a `${NAME:-...}` / `${NAME:=...}` / `$NAME` / `os.environ` read) by a shipped `install.sh` / `scripts/` / `lib/` file AND is declared in a consumer-facing document. The consumer sets it in a shell profile or an install one-liner.
criterion.A2_doc_declaration_rationale: The doc-declaration clause is what makes A2 select the OPERATOR surface rather than the harness. The read-and-never-internally-assigned mechanics alone select 25 names, almost all of them internal tuning knobs no consumer has ever been told about (DEVFLOW_REFRESH_*, DEVFLOW_TELEMETRY_MAX_*, DEVFLOW_GH_WRAPDIR, DEVFLOW_RECORDER_*, ...). An advisory that raised those to the same salience as DEVFLOW_APP_ID would bury the six names that actually matter. A name a consumer was never told to set cannot be a name a consumer renames.
criterion.never_assigned_internally: A2's never-assigned-internally clause is applied as a RECORDED ADJUDICATION per candidate rather than as a third grep, because a single name can be internally supplied to one reader and operator-supplied to another. DEVFLOW_REF is exactly that: `.github/actions/vendor-plugin/action.yml` assigns it for vendor-slice.sh's fetch branch, while `install.sh` reads it from the operator's own environment. A blanket assignment grep would delete DEVFLOW_REF from the consumer surface on the strength of a producer that never reaches install.sh. Every candidate the arms select is therefore resolved into `identifiers` or `adjudicated_out`, with the deciding evidence written down.

env_identifiers.pair_asymmetry: The asymmetry inverts what a careful consumer would guess. Rename the SECRET alone and the mint step fails loudly -- you find out immediately. Rename the VARIABLE alone and nothing fails: the mint is gated on `vars.<NAME> != ''`, an unresolvable name reads exactly like `deliberately not configured`, so every job falls back to `steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` and the run goes GREEN under a degraded identity. Rename BOTH -- the natural thing to do, since they are one setting in the consumer's head -- and the variable's silent skip gates off the secret's loud guard, so the loud half never runs. The safe rename order is therefore the one nobody would guess, which is the reason this block exists.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_APP_ID
identifiers.set_where: GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables
identifiers.read_as: vars.DEVFLOW_APP_ID -- both the `if:` gate on every App-token mint and the mint step's own `client-id:`
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent feature loss, the largest blast radius here. Every mint gate reads `vars.DEVFLOW_APP_ID != ''`, so an unresolvable name turns every gate false and every consumer falls back to `steps.app-token.outputs.token || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`. The run stays green. What breaks is all downstream and none of it names the cause: pushes touching `.github/workflows/` are rejected with `refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow ... without workflows permission` (which reads as a missing App permission, and the App permission is fine); the credential refresher still reports `credential refresher started (detached)` while its empty-input arm writes `cannot mint` into a redirected log nobody reads, so long implement runs die on an expired token with no trace; and PR authorship and review attribution move to `github-actions[bot]`, which does not satisfy a branch-protection required-approval rule.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
identifiers.set_where: GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Secrets
identifiers.read_as: secrets.DEVFLOW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, inside the mint step that `vars.DEVFLOW_APP_ID` gates
identifiers.failure_visibility: loud, but only while its paired variable still resolves
identifiers.failure_mode: The mint step fails loudly with an unusable private key -- provided `vars.DEVFLOW_APP_ID` still resolves and the step therefore runs at all. Rename the variable as well and the gate is already false, the mint never executes, and this loud guard is gated off: see `pair_asymmetry`.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_APP_ID
identifiers.set_where: GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables
identifiers.read_as: vars.DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_APP_ID -- the gate that decides whether the separate read-only DevFlow-Reviewer App identity is used at all
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent identity reversion. This is the GATING half of the reviewer pair: unresolvable, the reviewer mint is skipped exactly as if you had chosen not to configure a reviewer App, and review attribution falls back to the default token. Nothing reports it, and a branch-protection rule that requires an approval from a non-`github-actions[bot]` identity silently stops being satisfiable.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_PRIVATE_KEY
identifiers.set_where: GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Secrets
identifiers.read_as: secrets.DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_PRIVATE_KEY, inside the mint step that `vars.DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_APP_ID` gates
identifiers.failure_visibility: loud, but only while its paired variable still resolves
identifiers.failure_mode: The reviewer mint fails loudly with an unusable private key -- provided `vars.DEVFLOW_REVIEWER_APP_ID` still resolves. Rename the variable too and the gate is false, the mint is skipped, and the loud guard never runs: see `pair_asymmetry`.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_PROVIDER_API_KEY
identifiers.set_where: GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Secrets
identifiers.read_as: secrets.DEVFLOW_PROVIDER_API_KEY -- an explicit emptiness guard in the provider-routing step, and the `anthropic_api_key:` the action receives on the provider path
identifiers.failure_visibility: loud on the provider path; unread otherwise
identifiers.failure_mode: If a config section sets `provider`, the run refuses with an `::error::` naming DEVFLOW_PROVIDER_API_KEY -- the one cloud row that fails loudly on its own. If no section routes through a third-party provider the secret is never read, so a rename is invisible until the day you opt into provider routing, at which point the error names a secret you believe you have set.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_RUNNER
identifiers.set_where: GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables
identifiers.read_as: runs-on: ${{ vars.DEVFLOW_RUNNER && (...) || 'ubuntu-latest' }} -- directly on devflow-implement.yml's claude job and every devflow-retrospective.yml job, and as the fallback tail of the DEVFLOW_LIGHT_RUNNER expression on the light jobs (devflow.yml config/review_dedupe/gate/review_finalize and the command job's non-review branch, devflow-implement.yml config/gate)
identifiers.failure_mode: SILENT RUNNER RELOCATION, and the highest-severity outcome in this table. Unresolvable, the expression takes its `|| 'ubuntu-latest'` arm and EVERY job silently moves to a GitHub-hosted runner. That same job carries `secrets.DEVFLOW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` and `secrets.DEVFLOW_PROVIDER_API_KEY` in its environment -- so a consumer who self-hosts for network isolation or compliance has their GitHub App private key and their model-provider API key executed OUTSIDE the boundary they chose self-hosting for. Nothing errors, no job fails, and no log line names the cause; the only visible difference is the runner label in a page nobody re-reads after setup. Note the contrast with a MIS-SET value: a `DEVFLOW_RUNNER` that begins `[` but is not valid JSON fails loud at evaluation time. It is the name going missing, not the value being wrong, that is silent.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_LIGHT_RUNNER
identifiers.set_where: GitHub -> Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables
identifiers.read_as: runs-on: ${{ vars.DEVFLOW_LIGHT_RUNNER && (...) || (<DEVFLOW_RUNNER chain>) }} -- on the light jobs of the two comment-driven shipped workflows (devflow.yml config/review_dedupe/gate/review_finalize, devflow-implement.yml config/gate) and, gated on a standalone /prflow:review, devflow.yml's command job. Unset or empty, each expression falls back to the DEVFLOW_RUNNER chain (DEVFLOW_RUNNER's value, else ubuntu-latest)
identifiers.failure_mode: SILENT RUNNER RELOCATION of the light jobs only. The name going missing does not error: each light expression takes its DEVFLOW_RUNNER-chain fallback arm, so the light jobs revert to wherever DEVFLOW_RUNNER points (or ubuntu-latest when that too is unset) -- exactly the pre-opt-in placement. The visible symptom is a helper job billing an 8-core minute again, never a job failure or a log line naming the cause. As for DEVFLOW_RUNNER, a MIS-SET value that begins `[` but is not valid JSON fails loud at evaluation time; it is the name going missing, not the value being wrong, that is silent.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_BASH
identifiers.set_where: your shell profile, or the invocation that launches the runner
identifiers.read_as: honored at the invocation boundary (deliberately not a resolver -- a sourced resolver would itself need a chosen bash to run); `lib/preflight.sh` surfaces it in its `devflow-bash:` breadcrumb
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent reversion to whichever bash the host happens to select. On a healthy POSIX-bash host that is a no-op, so the rename looks successful; on the Windows host the override existed for, the shell helpers go back to running under whatever the launcher picks, and the preflight remedy naming WSL/Git Bash/MSYS2 bash returns.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_GH
identifiers.read_as: `: "${DEVFLOW_GH:=$(devflow_resolve_gh)}"` in every gh-calling shell helper; a non-empty value wins outright and is never probed
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent PATH reversion, and the worst kind of silent: on a host where the probe already finds a working `gh` the rename changes nothing observable, so the consumer concludes it worked. On the Windows/WSL host the override existed for, it silently restores the shadowing-`gh` bug the override was added to route around -- a present-but-unrunnable `gh` shim is selected again, and every `gh` call degrades to its best-effort empty-result path.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_JQ
identifiers.read_as: `: "${DEVFLOW_JQ:=$(devflow_resolve_bin jq)}"` in every jq-calling shell helper; a non-empty value wins outright and is never probed
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent PATH reversion, identical in shape to DEVFLOW_GH: a no-op on a host whose probe already resolves a working `jq`, so the rename appears to have worked, and a silent return of the shadowed-binary problem on the host that needed the override.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_REF
identifiers.dual_role: Also an INTERNAL input: `.github/actions/vendor-plugin/action.yml` assigns DEVFLOW_REF for vendor-slice.sh's fetch branch, sourced from the consumer's `prflow_version`. That internal producer never reaches install.sh, so the name is consumer-facing here and internal there. It is not purely one or the other.
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent un-pin. Unresolvable, install.sh takes its `:-main` default and clones mutable `main` instead of the tag you named. The install succeeds, reports a version, and stamps `prflow_version` -- with a ref you did not choose. A consumer pinning a known-good release to avoid an upgrade gets the upgrade, and the only evidence is the version the installer echoes.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_SRC
identifiers.set_where: the install one-liner -- `DEVFLOW_SRC=<dir> bash devflow-install.sh` -- to install from an already-materialized plugin tree instead of cloning
identifiers.read_as: `SRC="$DEVFLOW_SRC"` guarded by `[ -n "${DEVFLOW_SRC:-}" ]` in install.sh, which then skips the clone
identifiers.dual_role: Also set INTERNALLY by `/prflow:init`'s workflow-install step, which passes the installed plugin tree as DEVFLOW_SRC so install.sh installs from it with no network clone. That producer does reach install.sh, but a consumer running install.sh by hand still sets it themselves, so the name is consumer-facing here and internally supplied there.
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent reversion to a network clone. Unresolvable, install.sh's `[ -n ... ]` guard is false and it clones from GitHub instead of installing from the local tree you pointed at -- an air-gapped or offline install then fails to fetch, and a pinned local tree is silently replaced by whatever the clone resolves.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_VENDOR
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent mode reversion to a thin install. The plugin tree stops being committed and is fetched at runtime instead, which is the opposite of what a consumer who set this wanted -- typically an air-gapped or supply-chain-pinned repository. The installer says `thin install: the plugin is fetched at runtime`, which is a truthful line that reads as normal output rather than as a setting having been lost.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_DRY_RUN
identifiers.read_as: `[ "${DEVFLOW_DRY_RUN:-}" = "1" ]` in install.sh, which forces the preview mode request
identifiers.failure_visibility: silent, and the only row that WRITES as a result
identifiers.failure_mode: The only name here whose rename causes a WRITE. On a FIRST-TIME install the default mode is apply, so the preview you explicitly asked for silently becomes an apply and the installer writes to your repository. (On an existing install the default is already preview, so there the rename is a silent no-op.) The equivalent flag `--dry-run` is unaffected -- an unknown flag is rejected outright, which is exactly the loudness the environment channel lacks.

identifiers.name: DEVFLOW_APPLY
identifiers.read_as: `[ "${DEVFLOW_APPLY:-}" = "1" ]` in install.sh, which forces the apply mode request
identifiers.failure_mode: Silent no-write on an upgrade. An existing install defaults to preview, so the upgrade you believe you applied only previewed: the repository is unchanged and keeps running the previous workflows and the previous pin. The run exits 0 and its last line is the ordinary dry-run notice. The equivalent `--apply` flag is unaffected.

adjudicated_out.name: DEVFLOW_PROMPT_EXTENSION_ROOT
adjudicated_out.selected_by: A2 (read by scripts/load-prompt-extension.sh; declared in the consumer-facing docs)
adjudicated_out.evidence: Workflow-written and consumer-read-never: `.github/workflows/devflow.yml`, `devflow-runner.yml` (and `matcher-probe.yml`) ASSIGN it, and the sole shipped reader consults it only on the branch those workflows drive. A consumer never sets it, so there is nothing for a consumer to rename. It appears in the docs precisely to explain that the cloud workflows running the review engine set it -- which is the sentence a hand-drawn list mistakes for a declaration. Issue #1075 added the devflow.yml assignment; the verdict is unchanged, because it turns on a consumer never setting the variable rather than on how many workflows do.

adjudicated_out.name: DEVFLOW_CONFIG_FILE
adjudicated_out.evidence: It satisfies A2's read mechanics (`lib/config-source.sh` reads `${DEVFLOW_CONFIG_FILE:-...}` and no non-test file assigns it) but is declared in NONE of the consumer-facing documents. It is a test and tooling seam that was never published as a consumer setting, so no consumer has been told to set it and none can rename it. This is the boundary case the doc-declaration clause exists to decide; recorded explicitly so a later reader sees a decision rather than an omission. If it is ever documented as a consumer override, that same change moves it into `identifiers`.

adjudicated_out.name: DEVFLOW_TRIGGERING_USER
adjudicated_out.selected_by: A2 (read by scripts/apply-pr-triggerer.sh; declared in the consumer-facing docs)
adjudicated_out.evidence: Workflow-written and consumer-read-never, the same shape as DEVFLOW_PROMPT_EXTENSION_ROOT: `.github/workflows/devflow-implement.yml` ASSIGNS it from `github.event.sender.login` onto the writer step, and the sole shipped reader (`scripts/apply-pr-triggerer.sh`) consults it only on the cloud tier -- the branch that workflow drives. The local tier never reads it at all; it resolves the authenticated login through `gh api user` instead. A consumer never sets it, so there is nothing for a consumer to rename, and no honest `set_where` exists to write in an `identifiers` row: the value is derived from the trigger event, and a consumer-supplied one would be an identity the authorization step never vetted. It appears in the consumer-facing docs precisely to explain that the implement workflow propagates it -- the sentence a hand-drawn list mistakes for a declaration. Absence is deliberately NOT the silent-feature-loss class that makes a name consumer-facing here: an empty value on the cloud tier is the documented deployment-skew path, and the helper fail-closes on it -- it substitutes no other account (not the token owner, the App identity, or GITHUB_ACTOR), emits `assignment: skipped no-triggering-user`, and Phase 3.1.1 records a `dropped-failed` workpad reflection naming the skip, so the loss is visible in the run's own durable record rather than silent. Issue #1165 introduced it.

adjudicated_out.name: DEVFLOW_REFRESH_SELFTEST_FAILED
adjudicated_out.selected_by: A2 (read by scripts/stop-refresher.sh and scripts/refresher-selftest.sh; declared in docs/internal/cloud-setup.md)
adjudicated_out.evidence: An internal refresher marker path, workflow-written and consumer-set-never, the same shape as DEVFLOW_TRIGGERING_USER: the writer workflows' Start step assigns it (passing it to refresher-selftest.sh) and the Stop step derives it from the same HANDLE, while the shipped reader (scripts/stop-refresher.sh) consults it only on that workflow-driven teardown path. A consumer never sets it, so there is nothing for a consumer to rename. It appears in docs/internal/cloud-setup.md (issue #1925) precisely to explain that the Stop step derives the self-test marker path itself now that the writer workflows no longer publish it job-wide -- the sentence the doc-declaration clause exists to adjudicate, not a consumer setting.

adjudicated_out.name: DEVFLOW_REFRESH_REAP_GLOB
adjudicated_out.selected_by: A2 (read by scripts/stop-refresher.sh; declared in docs/internal/cloud-setup.md)
adjudicated_out.evidence: An internal test/override seam for the cross-job reaper, one of the DEVFLOW_REFRESH_* tuning knobs the A2_doc_declaration_rationale names as internal: scripts/stop-refresher.sh reads ${DEVFLOW_REFRESH_REAP_GLOB:-...} and, when it is unset, derives the pattern from a normalized RUNNER_TEMP instead. No shipped consumer surface sets it -- the workflows never pass it, and it exists so the test suite can scope the reaper. It appears in docs/internal/cloud-setup.md (issue #1925) only to explain that an explicitly-supplied pattern is used verbatim while the derived default is normalized -- an explanation of the mechanism, not a consumer setting.

frozen._comment: record_paths are RELATIVE TO THE STATE DIRECTORY: they move with it, and their bytes are never rewritten (they are append-only history and frozen census snapshots, so an edit falsifies the record). env_identifiers is issue #1004's Tier 3 record -- an inventory of DEVFLOW_* names that are NOT renamed, never a rename table. The DevFlow label, the devflow-telemetry branch and the <!-- devflow:* --> comment markers left this block in Tier 2 (#1003) and now live in the top-level identifiers block; the subagent-override namespace (devflow:<agent>) and the transitional /devflow:<command> spellings stay frozen, which is why the marker rule carries the HTML comment token rather than a bare devflow: prefix.

retained_helpers_deletion_condition.condition: These helpers were called only by the withheld auto-review tier's workflows (devflow-review.yml -> devflow-runner.yml). Issue #936 withheld the tier and issue #2071 removed its dead config settings, but the helpers stay in the tree so an installed consumer copy that still carries devflow-review.yml keeps resolving them. They are deleted in the first release after the maintainer has confirmed no installed consumer still carries a devflow-review.yml/devflow-runner.yml that calls them -- for example by walking every known consumer through the --remove-withheld-review-tier removal. Until that is confirmed the helpers stay; this is a confirmation to be made, not a date to wait for.

transitional_read_through.rule: A reader resolves the current state directory first. Only when that path is absent AND the superseded one is present does it fall back, and every such resolution writes a stderr breadcrumb naming /prflow:init. The fallback exists because a consumer's plugin can auto-update ahead of any migration run (init registers the marketplace with autoUpdate: true), so without it the very next plugin update would resolve an absent config and silently revert every `// default` extraction.
transitional_read_through.not_applies_reason: Issue #988 ruled out a read-through for the config keys: a silent key fallback makes the migration unobservable and therefore permanent. Key migration is detected instead -- scripts/config-get.sh's superseded-key breadcrumb and the workflow config jobs' per-family ::error:: guards.
transitional_read_through.end_criterion: The state-directory fallback is removed in the first release after the maintainer has walked every known consumer through /prflow:init and confirmed no repository still carries a .devflow/ directory. Until that is confirmed the fallback stays; it is not removed on a timer.
